title: Understanding SVD
text: In Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), the matrix X is decomposed into three matrices: U, S, and V. Each of these matrices has specific properties. For example, U and V are orthogonal matrices, and S is a diagonal matrix.

title: Properties of V
text: The matrix V in SVD represents the right singular vectors of X. These vectors are orthogonal and correspond to the directions of maximum variance in the data.

hintAnswer: The first row of V does not necessarily represent the direction of maximum variance.
title: Direction of Maximum Variance
text: Which row of V represents the direction of maximum variance in the data?
choices: The first row of V does not necessarily represent the direction of maximum variance.
The row corresponding to the largest singular value
